exposure: COVID-19 related restrictions (access to birthing units, presence of birthing partners)
cohort: 477 families in England who gave birth during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: The study found a higher proportion of birthing interventions (emergency CS) than previously reported, coupled with increased uncertainties, poor communication, heightened anxiety, and predominately negative emotions regarding birth experiences during the pandemic.
mod_finding: Two-thirds of women reported spontaneous vaginal delivery (66.1%) and one-third reported caesarean section (32.6%), with emergency CS being reported as higher than previously.
